note.title: Genetic disorders
note.overview: Different genetic disorders have different inheritance patterns, effects and management; accurate non-stigmatising language matters.
learningGoals: Recall the precise Year 8 vocabulary for genetic disorders.
Apply the knowledge rather than relying on recognition alone.
Use the command word and include every required scientific point.
mustMemoriseRules: Huntington's disease is linked to a dominant allele; sickle cell disease to a recessive allele; haemophilia is usually X-linked recessive; polydactyly is often dominant or a new mutation.
A carrier has an allele; the disorder is not the person's whole identity.
Management is not the same as cure.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.meaning: a progressive disorder associated with a dominant allele and movement, thinking, mood and coordination problems
a recessive haemoglobin disorder causing sickled red cells, anaemia, pain and blocked vessels
an inherited characteristic, often dominant or a new mutation, causing an extra finger or toe
a usually X-linked recessive disorder in which blood clots slowly

workedExamples.prompt: Why may a carrier not show sickle cell disease?
workedExamples.answer: The normal dominant allele masks the recessive disease allele in a heterozygous genotype.
